ui.title: One Belt, Many Lives
ui.intro: It is 2013, and China has just announced the Belt and Road. Watch the corridor from China to Europe change year by year, side by side with a shadow world where the plan never happened. Step into any life along the way to read their thoughts, and when they face a choice, whisper; they may not listen.
nudge.unavailable: Too late: they have already decided.

thought.displaced: Our land is gone. The compensation sits in the bank, but I don't know what to do with my hands.
thought.widowed: I still set out two cups in the morning. The house is so quiet now.
thought.child-born: The baby finally slept through the night. Everything costs more now, and I don't mind.
thought.job-lost: I keep waking at the old hour with nowhere to go. How long will the savings last?
thought.job: First weeks at the new job. I'm tired, but the pay comes on time.
thought.married: We're married now. Two families at one table; we'll learn each other's habits.
thought.moved: New street, new neighbours, and I still take the wrong turn to the shop. Maybe one day it will feel like home.
thought.retired: No alarm clock anymore. I thought I would enjoy it more than I do.
thought.decide.job-offer: They're hiring at the construction site. The money is good, but the work is hard and the dust never settles.
thought.decide.relocation: They say the new flats have running water and heating. But my parents are buried on this land.
thought.decide.protest: People are meeting in the square on Friday. If I go, will they remember my face? If I don't, will anything change?
thought.decide.emigrate: My cousin says there's work where he is. Could I really leave everyone behind?
thought.decide.bribe: He left an envelope on my desk and walked out. Nobody would ever know. I would.
thought.decide.speak-out: Someone should say out loud what's happening here. Why does it have to be me?
thought.pollution.bad: The dust from the cement works is back. The children cough at night.
thought.land.taken: Another family on our road signed the land papers this week. Who's next?
thought.danger: I don't walk home after dark anymore. Too many stories lately.
thought.debt.worried: They keep borrowing for bigger projects. Who pays it back, our children?
thought.jobs.appearing: There's work around here now: the depot, the new road, the warehouses. Even my nephew found something.
thought.china.hopeful: The new road cut my trip to the city in half. Whoever paid for it, it helps.
thought.china.wary: The contracts, the engineers, the money all come from far away. What stays here when they're done?
thought.economy.bad: Prices go up every month and my pay doesn't. Everyone at the market says the same.
thought.sanctions: The spare parts don't come anymore, and when they do, they cost three times as much.
thought.ordinary.child: If I finish my homework fast, maybe I can play football before dinner.
thought.ordinary.student: Exams in two weeks. Will a degree even get me a job?
thought.ordinary.homemaker: Rice, oil, school shoes. The money has to stretch to the end of the month.
thought.ordinary.retiree: My knees ache when it rains. The grandchildren are coming on Sunday.
thought.ordinary.unemployed: Another day asking around for work. Someone said the depot might need people.
thought.ordinary.farmer: If the rain comes on time, the harvest will be good this year.
thought.ordinary.herder: The grass is thin on the lower slopes. We'll have to take the flock higher soon.
thought.ordinary.fisher: The catch was small again this morning. Every year we go further out.
thought.ordinary.factory-worker: Twelve hours on the line, the same part a thousand times. At least the overtime pays.
thought.ordinary.miner: Down in the dark all day, I think about daylight. The pay keeps the family fed.
thought.ordinary.construction-worker: My back hurts from hauling rebar. When this bridge is done, where is the next job?
thought.ordinary.engineer: The drawings say one thing and the ground says another. The deadline doesn't care.
thought.ordinary.truck-driver: Three days to the border, and a day in the queue if I'm unlucky. I miss my kids.
thought.ordinary.rail-worker: The container trains keep getting longer. Someone still has to check every coupling.
thought.ordinary.dockworker: Another ship in at dawn. The cranes do more of the work now; how long will they need us?
thought.ordinary.sailor: Four months at sea. I count the ports until I'm home.
thought.ordinary.market-trader: Cheap goods keep arriving by the container. Good for my customers, harder for me.
thought.ordinary.shopkeeper: Slow day. Tomorrow is market day; it will pick up.
thought.ordinary.teacher: Thirty-five children in one room, and half of them want to be engineers now.
thought.ordinary.nurse: Another double shift. The ward needs more hands than it has.
thought.ordinary.office-worker: Meetings about meetings. Does anyone read the reports I write?
thought.ordinary.entrepreneur: If the new road really opens, I could double my deliveries. If it doesn't, I've borrowed for nothing.
thought.ordinary.customs-officer: The line of trucks stretches past the hill. Every driver wants to be first.
thought.ordinary.local-official: The capital wants the project finished before the anniversary. The villagers want answers I don't have.
thought.ordinary.bank-analyst: The loan numbers look fine on paper. I just wonder who checked the traffic forecasts.
thought.ordinary.port-manager: The new berth doubled our capacity. Now I need the ships to actually come.
